newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit extends gains on speculative buying.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit extends gains on speculative buying.

text.p: The ringgit extended gains made after Bank Negara's intervention on fresh dollar selling by speculators, dealers said on Wednesday.
They said the ringgit was expected to gain further in London and New York after the Kuala Lumpur and Singapore markets closed.
"At the moment those who have short the dollar at 2.5080 level are taking profit," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
Dealers said Bank Negara intervened in the foreign exchange market after the ringgit fell to a three-month low of 2.5120. It sold $100-200 million, which helped the ringgit recover.
There was no confirmation from Bank Negara, which does not usually comment on its market intervention operations.
At 0900 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5028/38 a dollar and at 1.7362/81 against the Singapore dollar.
"The central bank was acting through some large Malaysian banks. The intention seems to just slow down the ringgit's fall, not stop it," said a dealer with a large Malaysian bank.
Immediately after the intervention, the ringgit recovered 50 points to around 2.5060/70 a dollar. At 0300 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5080/90.
Support from the central bank also brought in Malaysian exporters, who had been waiting for dollar/ringgit's rise to sell their dollars, dealers said.
Bank Negara's action triggered an all round stop to ringgit selling and helped the Malaysian unit recover.

A U.S. hedge fund, squaring up a large three-month position in the ringgit, was said to be mainly responsible for the Malaysian currency's latest decline. The position is estimated to be in excess of two billion ringgit.
In addition, the strength of the U.S. dollar against the Japanese yen and other major currencies was also weakening regional currencies like the ringgit, dealers said.
"With the assumed presence of Bank Negara, there should be strong resistance at 2.51 level," a dealer with a European bank in Singapore said.
